newsitem.title: USA: US FCC changes airwave auction bidding rules.
newsitem.headline: US FCC changes airwave auction bidding rules.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Thursday adopted unified rules to cover future airwave auctions in a bid to simplify the process and speed the deployment of communications services to the public.
The agency -- which has conducted 12 spectrum auctions to date -- noted that in the past it has adopted new rules for each auction, slowing the overall auction process.
The FCC amended its competitive bidding rules to:
-- Include certain service-specific procedures, such as allowing the agency to clarify the extent of authority delegated to the head of the FCC wireless bureau.
-- Modify the short-form applications to include a certification that the applicant is not in default on any payment due to the FCC or of non-tax debt to a federal agency.
-- Clarified financial provisions in its rules that were the subject of petitions for reconsideration and requests for clarification.
The agency also will conduct a comprehensive review of its bidding rules in an effort to improve the application process and payment procedures, among other things.
